messages:
laura: Heads-up — we're seeing a sustained nvme queue depth spike on a subset of us-west1 accel nodes. GPU attach/hotstart times up ~2–4s and about 6% of attach attempts are timing out, causing provisioning backpressure.
sam: ugh. any correlation with scrub/janitor runs?
ingrid: yeah looks like Janitor runs started overlapping with nightly scrubs after the deploy. Cleaner concurrency jumped from 6 -> 18 around 01:10 UTC.
laura: here's an excerpt from iostat/nvme during the spike:

```
Device           r/s     w/s     rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s wrqm/s  avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1        1200.0  1800.0  51200   102400   0.00  0.00   45.22  9.12  1.21   12.34    0.80  96.8
```

nvme-cli shows heavy read/write queuing and retries.
ops-bot: Alert created: NVME_IO_QUEUE_DEPTH_SPIKE (severity: P2) — incident #2026-331
mike: Are these ephemeral scratch nodes used by batch jobs? Might be a specific tenant generating hotspot writes.
laura: Yes — two large batch shards were scheduled to the same hostpool. They coincide with the scrub window.
sam: Quick mitigation options:
- reduce janitor concurrency to 4 on affected pools (low effort)
- bump scrub spread window across more hours / shift to low-traffic window
- temporarily route new batch allocations to fallback pool with slightly higher cost
- increase io_credits throttle for scrub to avoid saturating device
ingrid: I can patch the janitor config now and iterate. Sam — can you open a quick PR to gate concurrency via feature flag so we can rollback fast?
sam: on it. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/janitor/PR-483
jyoti: Also worth checking KV cache behavior; heavy KV writes during attach can amplify queue depth. I can add kv cache hit-rate metric to the trace.
mike: Cost tradeoff note — moving to the fallback pool will raise per-attach cost ~12% but will keep SLAs. Ops prefers short-term cost > customer impacts.
laura: Ingrid patched janitor concurrency to 4 for us-west1 pools at 01:32. Metrics show queue depth dropped from 45 -> 6 in ~4 min and attach time returned to baseline.
ops-bot: Incident #2026-331 updated: mitigation applied — janitor concurrency reduced. Monitoring continue.
laura: Follow-ups:
- schedule scrub spread change (prod config) to avoid overlapping batch windows
- add a safeguard: prevent >2 concurrent heavy batch shards on same hostpool
- add a regression alert tying attach timeout rate to nvme queue depth
sam: I'll add the hostpool shard cap to the scheduler in a short changelist.
jyoti: I'll dashboard the KV write amplification and correlate with scrub runs.
mike: Thx — call out any nodes with persistent high SMART reallocated sectors, we should retire them early.
laura: good call. I'll run a quick scan and open retire tickets if needed. :thumbsup:
